key_insight: Independent benchmarking showed large performance differences among open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation tools, with domain-specific models generally outperforming foundation and general-purpose approaches.
clinical_relevance: More accurate and usable muscle segmentation can improve MRI-derived biomarkers used in neuromuscular disease research and potentially support more reliable clinical interpretation.
method: Compared eight open-source segmentation tools, including six standalone models and two auxiliary methods.
Evaluated performance on 3D MRI volumes from three base datasets and additional derived datasets.
Assessed both quantitative accuracy metrics and qualitative usability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports substantial variation across methods and datasets, with many tools performing worse on pathological cases and domain-specific models consistently leading the benchmark.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or disease patterns, so real-world deployment needs careful validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
